subject: Service impact: rw-small-ctx elevated timeouts — mitigation plan & timeline
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@starlite.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@starlite.ai
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: rw-small-ctx timeouts spike (started ~07:45 PST)

Hi Laura —

We're seeing a surge of 5xx / timeout errors from the rw-small-ctx model across multiple services starting ~07:45 PST. Error rate went from ~0.5% to ~12% for requests with context length > 1600 tokens. Failures show as 504 gateway timeouts in our logs and we also see repeated retried requests from the SDK.

Attached is a short export of request IDs and traces for the last 45 minutes. We have a production run at 09:00 PST that will be affected if this persists. Can Redwood confirm whether this is isolated to rw-small-ctx or a broader issue?

Attachments: starlite-logs-11-05.csv (text/csv, 42KB)

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Brooks
Head of Platform, Starlite AI
ops@starlite.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@starlite.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 08:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: rw-small-ctx timeouts spike (started ~07:45 PST)

Hi Evan — thanks for the heads up and for the log export. We're triaging now. Immediate notes:

- We've confirmed elevated 5xx/timeout rates for the rw-small-ctx model for requests with longer context lengths (matching what you observed).
- I've escalated to our infra and model ops teams and looped in Dev and Marcus for the root-cause and mitigation.
- Short-term mitigation (recommended): switch traffic to rw-small-ctx-v2 (backward-compatible variant) for the affected endpoints, and enable a temporary client-side retry with exponential backoff (max 3 attempts).

We should be able to push a routing rule within ~30 minutes if you want Redwood to handle the switch; alternatively you can change to the v2 model on your side. Let me know which you prefer and whether you want us to pause outgoing scheduled jobs until the patch.

I'll update in this thread as we have a technical RCA and a timeline for a fix.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@starlite.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: rw-small-ctx timeouts spike (started ~07:45 PST)

Hi Evan / Team — quick technical update from infra:

Summary of early findings:
- The spike is localized to the rw-small-ctx model family and correlates strongly with requests that have prefix lengths > 1600 tokens.
- Preliminary traces show long tail KV cache misses and memory churn on a subset of serving nodes causing token generation stalls and eventual gateway timeouts.

Immediate steps we've applied (09:00 PST):
1) Deployed a temporary routing rule to divert 50% of your traffic to rw-small-ctx-v2 (lower memory footprint).
2) Enabled stricter per-request memory guards on the affected pool and reduced the concurrent-request cap for nodes showing high memory pressure.
3) Instrumented additional tracing — I've attached a short diagnostic dump of a traced request for your reference.

Workarounds you can apply while we implement a permanent fix:
- Switch to rw-small-ctx-v2 for all production calls (recommended).
- If you cannot change model name immediately, add client-side retry with a 250–1000ms jittered backoff and fail-fast at 3 attempts.

I'll follow up with an RCA and ETA for the permanent remediation (likely a model runtime patch).

Attachments: rw-diagnostic-trace.txt (text/plain, 18KB)

—Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@starlite.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident update: rw-small-ctx timeout root cause & fix deployed

Hi Evan / Starlite team — final update and next steps.

Root cause: a regression in the KV cache eviction logic for rw-small-ctx under long-sequence workloads. For certain token-prefix distributions (those >~1600 tokens with repeated attention patterns) the runtime could enter a pathological cache-repopulation loop that caused sustained memory pressure and stalled generations. This manifested as timeouts and 5xxs on affected nodes.

What we did:
- Rolled out a runtime fix to the rw-small-ctx serving binary that corrects the eviction boundary and reduces cache-repopulation churn.
- Rebalanced affected nodes and cleared cache entries causing pressure.
- Completed a full validation pass across your production routes; error rates have returned to baseline (~0.6%).

Impact and timeline:
- Fix deployed and validated by 13:30 PST.
- Metrics indicate recovery window ~12:00–13:30 PST for the majority of traffic.

Recommended actions for Starlite:
- Migrate fully to rw-small-ctx-v2 where possible; v2 includes a hardened KV policy and stays resilient under long-sequence workloads.
- Keep client retry with capped attempts (3) and jittered backoff for transient errors.

Compensation: We will open an account review for a partial credit for the affected window (internal ticket INC-3245). I'll have Laura follow up on the details.

Attached: postmortem notes (internal) will be available in the Jira incident; link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-3245

If anything else pops up, please ping me directly.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Infrastructure Reliability, Redwood Inference
